addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- sprite: Use this skill when users are modifying system configuration, starting dev servers, requesting services (databases, Docker, Redis, etc.), installing dependencies or runtimes, or when they have made a functional change to their code that appears to be working (to create a checkpoint). Also use for managing checkpoints, restores, and understanding network policy in the Sprite VM.
- sprite-api-gateway: Use this skill when users want to access external APIs (GitHub, Slack, Linear, etc.), integrate with third-party services, or need authenticated API calls. The API gateway at api.sprites.dev handles authentication automatically — sprites never need raw API keys or tokens.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

Проверил — вот что реально в коммитах ветки `3`:

- Тестовый хардкод контактов вместо реального fetch: `[{name: 'Kate Bell', phone: '(555) 564-8583'}, {name: 'Yo', ...}, {name: 'Yo22', ...}]` — реальная логика закомментирована, а не удалена.
- `network_security_config.xml`, разрешающий cleartext-трафик на конкретный EC2-хост (`ec2-35-158-226-248...:7012`) — похоже на адрес старого dev/staging бэкенда.
- Дублированный вызов `directCall.unmuteMicrophone()` (два раза подряд) — похоже на случайный debug-артефакт, а не осознанное изменение.
- Мелкие правки: убран лишний `console.log`, исправлена опечатка в имени приложения (`'Caller App'` → `'Callme App'`), `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` permission убран, `targetApi` поднят с 28 до 35.

Итог: это не "пустые" коммиты — там реальные изменения, но по содержанию видно, что ветка использовалась как временный dev/debug-стенд (захардкоженные тестовые контакты, привязка к конкретному EC2 dev-серверу), а не как осмысленная фича-ветка. Так что "мусорный" в смысле "не нужно мержить как есть", а не в смысле "пустой diff" — приношу извинения за неточную формулировку раньше.

Единственное потенциально полезное: исправление опечатки `'Caller App'` → `'Callme App'` и снятие лишнего `console.log` — мелочи, которые могли бы попасть в основную ветку, но тривиальны и легко переделать заново.

Хотите, чтобы я так же подробно прошёлся по остальным веткам (не только по коммит-мессаджам), прежде чем удалять?

+# Guide: Moving Builds to External SSD
+
+This guide explains how to move heavy build directories and caches to an external SSD to save space and reduce wear on your internal drive.
+
+## 1. Preparation
+1. Plug in your SSD.
+2. Identify the mount path:
+   - **macOS**: `/Volumes/YourSSDName`
+   - **Linux**: `/media/user/YourSSDName` or `/mnt/ssd`
+3. Create a dedicated folder on the SSD for this project:
+   ```bash
+   mkdir -p /path/to/ssd/callme_external
+   ```
+
+---
+
+## 2. Node Modules (fe & web)
+The `node_modules` folders contain thousands of files.
+1. Delete existing folders (or move them):
+   ```bash
+   rm -rf fe/node_modules
+   rm -rf web/node_modules
+   ```
+2. Create folders on SSD and link them:
+   ```bash
+   mkdir -p /path/to/ssd/callme_external/fe_node_modules
+   ln -s /path/to/ssd/callme_external/fe_node_modules fe/node_modules
+
+   mkdir -p /path/to/ssd/callme_external/web_node_modules
+   ln -s /path/to/ssd/callme_external/web_node_modules web/node_modules
+   ```
+
+---
+
+## 3. iOS (macOS only)
+
+### 3.1 Xcode DerivedData
+Xcode stores all intermediate build files here. This can grow to 50GB+.
+1. Open **Xcode** > **Settings** (Cmd + ,) > **Locations**.
+2. Change **Derived Data** to a custom path on your SSD:
+   - Example: `/Volumes/YourSSDName/Xcode/DerivedData`
+
+### 3.2 CocoaPods (fe/ios/Pods)
+1. Delete existing Pods: `rm -rf fe/ios/Pods`
+2. Link to SSD:
+   ```bash
+   mkdir -p /path/to/ssd/callme_external/ios_pods
+   ln -s /path/to/ssd/callme_external/ios_pods fe/ios/Pods
+   ```
+
+---
+
+## 4. Android
+
+### 4.1 Global Gradle Cache
+Gradle downloads gigabytes of dependencies in `~/.gradle`.
+1. Move the folder:
+   ```bash
+   mv ~/.gradle /path/to/ssd/callme_external/.gradle
+   ```
+2. Create a link:
+   ```bash
+   ln -s /path/to/ssd/callme_external/.gradle ~/.gradle
+   ```
+*Alternatively, you can set `export GRADLE_USER_HOME="/path/to/ssd/callme_external/.gradle"` in your `.zshrc` or `.bashrc`.*
+
+### 4.2 Android Emulators (AVD)
+Virtual devices are stored in `~/.android/avd`.
+1. Move and link:
+   ```bash

+# Guide: Moving Builds to External SSD
+
+This guide explains how to move heavy build directories and caches to an external SSD to save space and reduce wear on your internal drive.
+
+## 1. Preparation
+1. Plug in your SSD.
+2. Identify the mount path:
+   - **macOS**: `/Volumes/YourSSDName`
+   - **Linux**: `/media/user/YourSSDName` or `/mnt/ssd`
+3. Create a dedicated folder on the SSD for this project:
+   ```bash
+   mkdir -p /path/to/ssd/callme_external
+   ```
+
+---
+
+## 2. Node Modules (fe & web)
+The `node_modules` folders contain thousands of files.
+1. Delete existing folders (or move them):
+   ```bash
+   rm -rf fe/node_modules
+   rm -rf web/node_modules
+   ```
+2. Create folders on SSD and link them:
+   ```bash
+   mkdir -p /path/to/ssd/callme_external/fe_node_modules
+   ln -s /path/to/ssd/callme_external/fe_node_modules fe/node_modules
+
+   mkdir -p /path/to/ssd/callme_external/web_node_modules
+   ln -s /path/to/ssd/callme_external/web_node_modules web/node_modules
+   ```
+
+---

+Xcode stores all intermediate build files here. This can grow to 50GB+.
+1. Open **Xcode** > **Settings** (Cmd + ,) > **Locations**.
+2. Change **Derived Data** to a custom path on your SSD:
+   - Example: `/Volumes/YourSSDName/Xcode/DerivedData`
+
+### 3.2 CocoaPods (fe/ios/Pods)

+2. Link to SSD:

+   ```
+
+---
+
+## 4. Android
+
+### 4.1 Global Gradle Cache
+Gradle downloads gigabytes of dependencies in `~/.gradle`.
+1. Move the folder:
+   ```bash

+   ```

+   ```

content.text:
**1) `visualizernstuff`**

Единственный уникальный коммит там — `c3edad4 "smth"`, лежит прямо поверх `458cffa` (это уже давно часть main). Внутри:
- `shared/store/contacts/types.ts`: добавляет `avatar_url` / `app_avatar_url` в `Contact` — **та же самая идея**, что и в `unpushed`/переименованной `idea/contact-avatar-url` (один и тот же автор, близкая дата, почти идентичный диф).
- `fe/package.json`: убрана зависимость `react-native-international-phone-number`.
- `fe/yarn.lock`: просто пересборка лок-файла (9967 строк — это шум от удаления пакета, не контент).

Т.е. `visualizernstuff` — это по сути дубль `idea/contact-avatar-url`, только с довеском в виде удаления одного пакета. Ничего нового по сравнению с уже сохранённой веткой. Могу удалить, если не нужно.

**2) `refactor/native-modules-to-expo-modules` vs main**

Да, форкнулась из той же точки `ef53ae3` (пре-relay), что и main сейчас. Реальный (не build-artifact) контент сверху:

- **Face-mask нативный модуль для iOS**: `AppDelegate.swift`, `MediaPipeFaceLandmarkerPlugin.swift/.m`, bridging header, `face_landmarker.task` (модель MediaPipe, 3.7MB) — это нативная (Swift/ObjC) сторона фичи face-mask. Похоже, дополняет `feature/face-mask-frame-guard` (у той — только 1 коммит, вероятно JS-сторона), а не дублирует.
- **`web/src/store/calls/index.ts` + `be/.env`**: коммит "Connect web signaling socket to ws path" — фикс сигналинга для веб-звонков.
- **`be/app/services/otp.py` + `be/.env`**: "Enable local OTP test configuration" — тестовый OTP-конфиг для локальной разработки.

Confirmed — `android-widget-wip` targets the old native package (`com.youshoudlcallme.app`), which no longer exists in `main` at all. Here's the breakdown of all three:

**`fix/shared-module-types`** — web-only rewrite. Both its commits ("Refactor call signaling relay" + "Fix shared module type resolution") touch exclusively `web/` and `shared/` — nothing in `fe/` (mobile) or `be/` (backend). This is your "strict relay" experiment, but scoped just to the web client: rewrites `web/src/store/calls/index.ts` (386 lines), touches web auth/navigation/contacts screens, and adds `web/src/types/js-modules.d.ts` (the "shared module type" fix). So it's an alternate web-side call-handling implementation, not a backend relay change.

**`experiment/drop-pending-call-buffering`** — backend + resilience work, 6 commits. This one's real and self-contained: removes server-side offer/ICE buffering from `be/app/ws/manager.py` / `routes.py` in favor of client-side retry (`web/src/store/calls/index.ts`, `fe/store/calls.ts`), plus two bug fixes around restoring user availability on WebSocket disconnect / pending-offer expiry. Small, focused, backend-touching — this is the one closest to a mergeable improvement.

**`android-widget-wip`** — dead. Targets the pre-Expo-modules Android project (`com.youshoudlcallme.app` package, manual `ContactsWidget.java`), which was fully replaced by `fe/modules/expo-widgets/` (Kotlin, `expo.modules.widgets` package) already sitting in `main`. Old package name doesn't exist anywhere in `main` anymore. Only thing possibly worth a glance: it bundles custom fonts (`InnovatorGrotesk-*.otf`) and a widget layout redesign, if you ever want visual-design ideas for the current widget — but the code itself can't apply as-is.

My take: `experiment/drop-pending-call-buffering` is the strongest candidate to actually merge into `main` next (small, backend-relevant, addresses real ICE-disconnect bugs). `fix/shared-module-types` needs a decision on whether the web client should get its own signaling implementation. `android-widget-wip` is safe to delete now that I've confirmed it's fully superseded.

=== CALL_SIGNALING_FLOW.md (new doc on this branch) ===
# Call Signaling Flow

Документ описывает текущую схему звонков после рефактора на `callee_ready`, а
также старую схему, которая была до этого изменения.

## Коротко

После рефактора backend разделен на две роли:

- REST API владеет lifecycle звонка: создать invite, принять, отклонить,
  отменить, завершить, поменять availability и отправить fallback push.
- WebSocket является live relay: он только пересылает online-сообщения между
  двумя телефонами.

WebSocket больше не хранит SDP offer и ICE candidates. Если получатель не
подключен к `/ws`, backend возвращает отправителю `delivery_failed`.

Главное изменение протокола: caller не создает WebRTC offer сразу. Сначала
callee должен получить invite, поднять WebSocket и отправить caller-у
`callee_ready`. Только после этого caller создает `RTCPeerConnection`, SDP
offer и ICE candidates.

## Базовые сущности

### `CallInvite`

Backend хранит ringing-звонок в таблице `db_callinvite`.

Важные поля:

- `call_id`: UUID звонка, который генерирует клиент. В REST он передается как
  `call_uuid`, в WS как `callId`.
- `caller_phone` и `callee_phone`: canonical identity обеих сторон.
- `status`: `ringing`, `accepted`, `rejected`, `cancelled`, `ended`, `expired`.
- `expires_at`: TTL ringing-звонка, сейчас 60 секунд.

REST lifecycle endpoints идемпотентны по `call_uuid`. Если один и тот же
`reject`, `cancel` или `end` прилетит повторно, backend не сделает второй push и
не применит переход второй раз.

### WebSocket identity

Клиент регистрируется так:

```json
{ "type": "register", "token": "<bearer-token>" }
```

Backend достает `User.phone` из токена и хранит online connection как:

```text
phone -> WebSocket
```

Все `to` / `from` в WebSocket сообщениях являются телефонами, а не SQL id.

## Текущая система

### 1. Callee online в web

1. Caller вызывает `POST /api/calls/initiate` с `callee_phone` и `call_uuid`.
2. Backend создает `CallInvite(status="ringing")`.
3. Backend помечает caller unavailable.
4. Backend видит, что callee подключен к WS, и отправляет ему:

   ```json
   {
     "type": "incoming_call",
     "call_id": "<uuid>",
     "call_uuid": "<uuid>",
     "caller_phone": "+...",
     "caller_id": "+..."
   }
   ```

5. Для web backend не отправляет web push, если WS-доставка уже успешна.
6. Web callee сохраняет invite локально и отправляет caller-у:

   ```json
   { "type": "callee_ready", "to": "+caller", "callId": "<uuid>" }

### `CallInvite`

Backend хранит ringing-звонок в таблице `db_callinvite`.

Важные поля:

- `call_id`: UUID звонка, который генерирует клиент. В REST он передается как
  `call_uuid`, в WS как `callId`.
- `caller_phone` и `callee_phone`: canonical identity обеих сторон.
- `status`: `ringing`, `accepted`, `rejected`, `cancelled`, `ended`, `expired`.
- `expires_at`: TTL ringing-звонка, сейчас 60 секунд.

REST lifecycle endpoints идемпотентны по `call_uuid`. Если один и тот же
`reject`, `cancel` или `end` прилетит повторно, backend не сделает второй push и
не применит переход второй раз.

### WebSocket identity

Клиент регистрируется так:

```json
{ "type": "register", "token": "<bearer-token>" }
```

Backend достает `User.phone` из токена и хранит online connection как:

```text
phone -> WebSocket
```

Все `to` / `from` в WebSocket сообщениях являются телефонами, а не SQL id.

## Текущая система

### 1. Callee online в web

1. Caller вызывает `POST /api/calls/initiate` с `callee_phone` и `call_uuid`.
2. Backend создает `CallInvite(status="ringing")`.
3. Backend помечает caller unavailable.
4. Backend видит, что callee подключен к WS, и отправляет ему:

   ```json
   {
     "type": "incoming_call",
     "call_id": "<uuid>",
     "call_uuid": "<uuid>",
     "caller_phone": "+...",
     "caller_id": "+..."
   }
   ```

5. Для web backend не отправляет web push, если WS-доставка уже успешна.
6. Web callee сохраняет invite локально и отправляет caller-у:

   ```json
   { "type": "callee_ready", "to": "+caller", "callId": "<uuid>" }

content.text:
Correcting myself — this is far more substantial than my earlier (truncated) diffstat suggested. It's a genuine, well-documented protocol redesign:

- **New `CallInvite` DB model + migration** (`be/alembic/versions/0002_call_invites.py`) — no conflict with main's schema (main only has `0001_initial`).
- **Architecture split**: REST now owns call lifecycle (invite/accept/reject/cancel/end, idempotent by `call_uuid`, 60s ringing TTL, offline push fallback); WebSocket becomes a pure online relay — no longer buffers SDP offers/ICE candidates.
- **Protocol fix**: caller no longer creates the WebRTC offer immediately — waits for callee's `callee_ready` over WS first. This is consistently implemented across `be/`, `fe/` (mobile), *and* `web/`, plus a 343-line `CALL_SIGNALING_FLOW.md` documenting it in Russian.

This is not a half-finished experiment — it reads like a deliberate, complete redesign.

**Is it safe to merge?** Mechanically, no — a real test-merge conflicts on 10 files (`be/app/api/calls.py`, `be/app/ws/manager.py`, `be/app/ws/routes.py`, `fe/api/index.ts`, `calling-screen.tsx`, `fe/lib/calls/android.ts`, `fe/lib/calls/ios.ts`, `fe/lib/notifications/remote.ts`, `fe/store/calls.ts`, `web/src/store/calls/index.ts`) because `main`'s current call code (from the `codex/call-notification-logging` merge) independently touched the same files without this protocol. It needs a deliberate manual reconciliation — likely keeping this branch's protocol/architecture as the base and re-applying `codex`'s debug-logging on top, rather than a quick merge. I'd treat it as a real integration task, not a button-push. Want me to attempt that reconciliation now, or hold off until you've tested `experiment/drop-pending-call-buffering` (since both touch the same backend WS/call files and you're still deciding on that one)?

content.text:
Now I have the full picture. Answering your question directly:

**Нет, Aeonik не нужен** — сейчас основной (и единственный) шрифт всего приложения — это **InnovatorGrotesk**. `fe/app/_layout.tsx` грузит только его 4 веса (regular/medium/semibold/bold) через `expo-font`, и все компоненты (`fontFamily.regular/medium/semibold/bold` из `@/utils/typography`) ссылаются именно на них. AeonikFonoTRIAL нигде в JS-коде не используется — он лежит только как файлы под `fe/android/.../assets/fonts/` и `res/font/` (нативная Android-сторона), похоже, из более старой попытки/эксперимента, но приложение сейчас его не подключает через `useFonts`. Так что для виджетов правильный выбор — InnovatorGrotesk, в соответствии с остальным приложением.

Продолжаю: подключаю InnovatorGrotesk к виджетам, используя уже имеющийся в `main` полный набор весов (`fe/assets/fonts/IG/`), удаляю `android-widget-wip`.

content.text:
Разница в философии, не просто в объёме кода:

**`experiment/drop-pending-call-buffering`** — точечный патч поверх текущей архитектуры. Звонок как раньше: caller сразу шлёт offer. Раньше, если callee offline, сервер держал offer+ICE в памяти (`pending_calls`/`pending_candidates`) и отдавал их при коннекте. Тут это убрано — вместо этого сервер просто отвечает `user_offline`, а **клиент** сам ретраит: таймер каждые 4с пересылает offer заново, до 15 попыток, с периодическим ICE-restart (на случай смены сети). Плюс 2 багфикса вокруг восстановления availability при дисконнекте. Итого 4 файла, без миграций БД, риск минимальный.

**`fix/shared-module-types`** — решает ту же проблему (гонка "offer отправлен раньше, чем callee реально готов его принять"), но убирая причину, а не симптом. Вводит `CallInvite` в БД, переносит весь lifecycle звонка на REST (idempotent invite/accept/reject/cancel/end, TTL 60с, push-фоллбек), а WS превращает в чистый relay. Главное: caller вообще не создаёт offer, пока не получит от callee явный `callee_ready` по WS — то есть по конструкции невозможна ситуация "офер улетел в пустоту". Затрагивает be+fe+web согласованно, есть даже отдельный документ-спека протокола.

**Что предпочтительнее:** архитектурно `fix/shared-module-types` мне кажется более правильным решением — он убирает саму гонку через явный handshake, а не гасит её ретраями с таймаутом (retry-loop это в сущности "подождать и понадеяться", а callee_ready — гарантия). Но это гораздо более крупный и рискованный шаг: новая таблица, переписанный REST-контракт, нужно валидировать на всех трёх клиентах разом. `drop-pending-call-buffering` — низкорисковый, узкий фикс, который можно протестировать и выкатить прямо сейчас независимо.

Если бы выбирал: тестировать `drop-pending-call-buffering` в ближайшей перспективе (что вы и планируете), но держать `fix/shared-module-types` в уме как "куда двигаться дальше", а не как конкурента прямо сейчас — это скорее следующий шаг эволюции, чем альтернатива тому же самому фиксу.

@router.post("/accept")
async def accept_call(
    data: AcceptCallRequest, callee: CurrentUser, session: SessionDep
) -> dict:
    caller_phone = _normalize_or_422(data.caller_phone)
    call_id = _request_call_id(data)
    _log_event("ACCEPT_START", caller_phone, callee.phone, call_uuid=call_id)

    result = await session.execute(select(User).where(User.phone == caller_phone))
    caller = result.scalar_one_or_none()
    if not caller:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Caller not found")

    invite = await _find_invite(
        session,
        call_id=call_id,
        caller_phone=caller.phone,
        callee_phone=callee.phone,
    )
    if not invite:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Call invite not found")
    if await _expire_if_needed(session, invite):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail="Call invite expired")

    changed = _mark_transition(invite, "accepted")
    if changed:
        callee.just_set_unavailable()
        await session.flush()
        await _notify_self_availability(callee, "User set as unavailable during call")

    notification_sent = False
    if changed:
        notification_sent = await _send_fallback_push_if_offline(
            session,
            user=caller,
            payload={
                "type": "call_accepted",
                "call_id": invite.call_id,
                "call_uuid": invite.call_id,
                "callee_phone": str(callee.phone) if callee.phone else "",
                "timestamp": _timestamp(),
            },
        )

    _log_event(
        "ACCEPT_SUCCESS",
        caller.phone,
        callee.phone,
        call_uuid=invite.call_id,
        changed=changed,
        notification_sent=notification_sent,
    )
    return {
        "success": True,
        "status": invite.status,
        "changed": changed,
        "notification_sent": notification_sent,
    }

content.text:
Оба замечания в точку, давай разберу.

**1) REST для lifecycle — не делает ли онлайн-кейс медленнее?**

Проверил код `accept_call` в `be/app/api/calls.py` и клиентский `acceptCall()` в `fe/store/calls.ts` этой ветки. Ответ: нет, не делает — и вот почему конкретно.

REST здесь не заменяет WS-доставку живых сигналов, а идёт **параллельно** ей:

```js
sendWsOnce('answer', targetId, currentCallId, { answer })  // сразу, по WS
if (targetId) {
  await sendRestOnce('accept', currentCallId, () => apiAcceptCall(targetId, currentCallId))  // после, не блокирует
}
```

`answer` (и `callee_ready`, и `offer`) как летели напрямую по WS между клиентами через relay, так и летят — без изменений в этой части. REST-вызов (`apiAcceptCall`) идёт следом, и его единственная задача — обновить durable-состояние `CallInvite` в БД (idempotency, TTL, офлайн-фоллбэк). Причём я посмотрел `_send_fallback_push_if_offline` — там явная проверка `is_connected(phone)`: если сторона онлайн через WS, пуш вообще не шлётся, ничего лишнего не происходит. Push/REST-путь используется буквально только когда WS-соединения нет — то есть ровно тогда, когда он и нужен. Так что в кейсе "оба онлайн" лишнего хопа в живом сигнальном пути нет — REST это side-channel bookkeeping, а не замена сокета.

**2) Гонка в offer-retry (drop-pending-call-buffering) — стейл-ответ на устаревший try**

Тут ты нашёл реальный edge case. Смотрел код: большинство ретраев (7 из 8) просто **пересылают тот же самый** `pc.localDescription` — offer не пересоздаётся, SDP идентичен. Поэтому ответ (`answer`), пришедший на "try #3", по факту относится к той же самой offer-сущности, что и try #1 — переговоры на уровне SDP от этого не портятся, это просто повторная отправка одних и тех же данных.

Настоящая уязвимость — именно на границе **ICE-restart** (каждый 8-й попыток, `ICE_RESTART_EVERY = 8`): там `pc.createOffer({iceRestart: true})` + `setLocalDescription` реально меняет offer (новые ICE ufrag/pwd). Если callee успел получить и обработать *старый* offer прямо перед этим рестартом, и его `answer` придёт caller-у уже **после** того как локально сгенерировался новый offer — код в кейсе `'answer'` делает `pc.setRemoteDescription(answer)` безусловно, без проверки "к какому поколению offer'а это относится". Answer на старый (pre-restart) SDP применится поверх уже нового локального description с другими ICE-credentials — рассинхрон, соединение скорее всего не установится корректно (mismatch по ufrag) или потребует ещё одного цикла.

Так что: для обычных ретраев риска нет (offer не меняется), а вот вокруг ICE-restart — да, гонка реальна, просто узкое окно (раз в 32 секунды) и нужно, чтобы answer от callee пришёл именно в этот момент. Не заблокирует нормальную работу в большинстве случаев, но именно такого рода "стейл в моменте рестарта" баг там есть, версионирования offer/answer пар (номер попытки/generation id) в коде нет.

Это ещё один аргумент в пользу `fix/shared-module-types`: там offer создаётся **один раз**, после явного `callee_ready`, без периодической регенерации — и этого класса гонки просто не существует по конструкции.

# Known issue: offer-retry vs. ICE-restart race

Applies to the client-side offer-retry loop introduced in this branch
(`experiment/drop-pending-call-buffering`), implemented in
`fe/store/calls.ts` (`startOfferRetry` / `sendOfferRetry`) and mirrored in
`web/src/store/calls/index.ts`.

## Background

This branch drops server-side buffering of offers/ICE candidates for
offline callees (`be/app/ws/manager.py`, `be/app/ws/routes.py`). Instead,
when the callee isn't connected, the backend just replies `user_offline`
and the **caller's client** retries: `sendOfferRetry()` resends the offer
every `OFFER_RETRY_INTERVAL` (4s), up to `MAX_OFFER_ATTEMPTS` (15), and
every `ICE_RESTART_EVERY`-th attempt (8) regenerates the offer via
`pc.createOffer({ iceRestart: true })` so a mid-ring network change
(Wi-Fi -> cellular) doesn't leave stale ICE candidates.

## The race

Most retries (7 out of 8) resend the exact same `pc.localDescription` — no
new SDP is generated, so an `answer` arriving in response to any of those
retries negotiates correctly regardless of which specific retry triggered
it.

The exception is the ICE-restart attempt: that one genuinely replaces
`pc.localDescription` with a new offer carrying new ICE `ufrag`/`pwd`.

If the callee receives and answers a **pre-restart** offer, but that answer
arrives back at the caller **after** the ICE-restart has already replaced
`pc.localDescription`, the caller's `case 'answer'` handler in
`fe/store/calls.ts` still applies it unconditionally:

```ts
case 'answer': {
  stopOfferRetry()
  const pc = get().pc
  if (pc) {
    await pc.setRemoteDescription(new RTCSessionDescription(msg.answer))
    ...
```

That `setRemoteDescription` call applies an answer negotiated against the
old ICE credentials onto a peer connection that has already moved to a new
generation of ICE credentials. The result is a mismatched local/remote ICE
credential pair, which can make the connection fail to establish or behave
inconsistently.

## Why it's narrow, not fixed here

- ICE-restart only happens every 8th attempt (~every 32s into a ring), so
  the race window only opens around that boundary.
- It requires the callee's answer for the specific pre-restart offer to be
  delayed enough to cross that boundary (e.g. backgrounded app resuming,
  network delay).
- No offer/answer generation tracking exists today — the code doesn't tag
  offers with a generation id and doesn't drop answers that don't match the
  current generation.

## Possible fixes

- Tag each offer (including ICE-restarted ones) with a generation id, and
  ignore/discard answers whose generation doesn't match
  `pc.localDescription`'s current generation.
- Adopt the explicit `callee_ready` handshake from `fix/shared-module-types`
  instead: there, the caller creates exactly one offer, only after the
  callee has confirmed it's ready to receive it — no retry loop, no
  regeneration, so this class of race can't occur by construction.

new SDP is generated, so an `answer` arriving in response to any of those
retries negotiates correctly regardless of which specific retry triggered
it.

The exception is the ICE-restart attempt: that one genuinely replaces
`pc.localDescription` with a new offer carrying new ICE `ufrag`/`pwd`.

If the callee receives and answers a **pre-restart** offer, but that answer
arrives back at the caller **after** the ICE-restart has already replaced
`pc.localDescription`, the caller's `case 'answer'` handler in
`fe/store/calls.ts` still applies it unconditionally:

```ts
case 'answer': {
  stopOfferRetry()
  const pc = get().pc
  if (pc) {
    await pc.setRemoteDescription(new RTCSessionDescription(msg.answer))
    ...
```

That `setRemoteDescription` call applies an answer negotiated against the
old ICE credentials onto a peer connection that has already moved to a new
generation of ICE credentials. The result is a mismatched local/remote ICE
credential pair, which can make the connection fail to establish or behave
inconsistently.

## Why it's narrow, not fixed here

- ICE-restart only happens every 8th attempt (~every 32s into a ring), so
  the race window only opens around that boundary.
- It requires the callee's answer for the specific pre-restart offer to be
  delayed enough to cross that boundary (e.g. backgrounded app resuming,
  network delay).
- No offer/answer generation tracking exists today — the code doesn't tag
  offers with a generation id and doesn't drop answers that don't match the
  current generation.

## Possible fixes

- Tag each offer (including ICE-restarted ones) with a generation id, and
  ignore/discard answers whose generation doesn't match
  `pc.localDescription`'s current generation.
- Adopt the explicit `callee_ready` handshake from `fix/shared-module-types`
  instead: there, the caller creates exactly one offer, only after the
  callee has confirmed it's ready to receive it — no retry loop, no
  regeneration, so this class of race can't occur by construction.

**`wip/alt-calls-store-incall-manager`** — альтернативный `store/calls2.ts` целиком построен вокруг **Sendbird Calls SDK**. А Sendbird полностью выпилен из приложения ещё в основной цепочке (`a7a15be "Remove legacy Sendbird and Jitsi references"`) в пользу кастомного WebRTC-сигналинга. Все методы (`renewSendbirdAccount`, `SendbirdCalls.authenticate` и т.д.) работают с API, которого в проекте больше нет. Паттерны InCallManager там даже менее полные, чем в текущем `fe/store/calls.ts` (просто закомментированы). Мёртвый груз.

**`wip/android-lock-screen-incoming-call-ui`** и **`wip/android-wake-screen-on-incoming-call`** — обе решают одну и ту же задачу (полноэкранный incoming-call поверх лок-скрина, будим экран) вручную: кастомная нативная `RedScreenActivity.java`, `BlueScreenComponent.js`, `notifee`-трюки (`fullScreenAction`, `visibility: PUBLIC`). Проверил `main` — там это уже решено через выделенный пакет `react-native-full-screen-notification-incoming-call`, и в `AndroidManifest.xml` уже стоят `android:showWhenLocked="true"` `android:turnScreenOn="true"` на нужных activity + разрешение `WAKE_LOCK`. **`wip/ios-callkeep-manual-podfile-link`** — ручная линковка CallKeep в `Podfile` (`pod 'RNCallKeep', :path => ...`) до появления Expo config-plugins. Main теперь линкует это автоматически через `@config-plugins/react-native-callkeep`. Никакого скрытого воркэраунда/фикса там нет — просто ручной эквивалент того, что сейчас генерируется автоматически.

# Contact avatars — design (deferred, needs S3)

Not implemented yet — this branch just captures the plan so it's ready to
pick up once S3 (or equivalent object storage) is set up.

## Existing dead code to be aware of

`fe/app/(app)/(home)/settings.tsx` already has an avatar upload UI
(`uploadAvatar`, image picker, placeholder-with-initials fallback) left over
from an earlier attempt. It's currently non-functional:

- It calls `POST /api/upload_avatar`, which does not exist anywhere in
  `be/app` — no route, no handler.
- `User.avatar_url` is referenced in `fe/store/auth.ts` and
  `shared/store/contacts/types.ts`, but the backend `User` model has no
  `avatar_url` column — nothing persists it.

When implementing this feature, reuse/fix that UI rather than building a
new one from scratch.

## Feature

Let a user set their own avatar. When displaying a contact (in the contacts
list, and on the incoming/outgoing call screen), resolve the image to show
with this priority:

1. **The photo the device's native Contacts app already has for that
   phone number.** Already available today, on-device, no backend or
   upload needed — this is the "you already know what they look like from
   your own address book" case, and should win whenever it's actually set,
   since it's the picture the user themself chose to associate with that
   contact.
2. **The avatar the other person set for themselves in-app**
   (`app_avatar_url`, uploaded by them, served from wherever we end up
   storing it — S3 or similar). Falls back to this when the local device
   doesn't have a photo for that number.
3. **Placeholder** (initials or generic icon — already exists in
   `settings.tsx`'s fallback) if neither of the above is available.

## What's blocked on S3

- Object storage for uploaded avatar images (S3 or equivalent).
- `be/app/api/*`: a real `/api/upload_avatar` endpoint (auth, upload to
  storage, return URL).
- DB migration: add `avatar_url` (or `app_avatar_url`, naming TBD) column
  to the `User` model.
- Wiring the returned URL back through `editUser({ avatar_url })` (already
  called from the existing dead UI in `settings.tsx`).

## What's not blocked (native contacts photo, priority #1)

Reading the local device Contacts app photo for a given phone number
doesn't need any of the above — can be implemented independently, ahead of
the S3-backed avatar upload, since it's a device-local read via the
existing contacts permission/adapter (`fe/store/contacts/adapter.ts`).

   your own address book" case, and should win whenever it's actually set,
   since it's the picture the user themself chose to associate with that

2. **The avatar the other person set for themselves in-app**
   (`app_avatar_url`, uploaded by them, served from wherever we end up
   storing it — S3 or similar). Falls back to this when the local device

# Contact avatars — design (deferred, needs S3)

Not implemented yet — this branch just captures the plan so it's ready to
pick up once S3 (or equivalent object storage) is set up.

## Existing dead code to be aware of

`fe/app/(app)/(home)/settings.tsx` already has an avatar upload UI
(`uploadAvatar`, image picker, placeholder-with-initials fallback) left over
from an earlier attempt. It's currently non-functional:

- It calls `POST /api/upload_avatar`, which does not exist anywhere in
  `be/app` — no route, no handler.
- `User.avatar_url` is referenced in `fe/store/auth.ts` and
  `shared/store/contacts/types.ts`, but the backend `User` model has no
  `avatar_url` column — nothing persists it.

When implementing this feature, reuse/fix that UI rather than building a
new one from scratch.

## Feature

Let a user set their own avatar. When displaying a contact (in the contacts
list, and on the incoming/outgoing call screen), resolve the image to show
with this priority:

1. **The photo the device's native Contacts app already has for that
   phone number.** Already available today, on-device, no backend or
   upload needed — this is the "you already know what they look like from
   your own address book" case, and should win whenever it's actually set,
   since it's the picture the user themself chose to associate with that
   contact.
2. **The avatar the other person set for themselves in-app**
   (`app_avatar_url`, uploaded by them, served from wherever we end up
   storing it — S3 or similar). Falls back to this when the local device
   doesn't have a photo for that number.
3. **Placeholder** (initials or generic icon — already exists in
   `settings.tsx`'s fallback) if neither of the above is available.

## What's blocked on S3

- Object storage for uploaded avatar images (S3 or equivalent).
- `be/app/api/*`: a real `/api/upload_avatar` endpoint (auth, upload to
  storage, return URL).
- DB migration: add `avatar_url` (or `app_avatar_url`, naming TBD) column
  to the `User` model.
- Wiring the returned URL back through `editUser({ avatar_url })` (already
  called from the existing dead UI in `settings.tsx`).

## What's not blocked (native contacts photo, priority #1)

Reading the local device Contacts app photo for a given phone number
doesn't need any of the above — can be implemented independently, ahead of
the S3-backed avatar upload, since it's a device-local read via the
existing contacts permission/adapter (`fe/store/contacts/adapter.ts`).

# Contact avatars — design

## Feature

Let a user set their own avatar. When displaying a contact (in the contacts
list, and on the incoming/outgoing call screen), resolve the image to show
with this priority:

1. **The photo the device's native Contacts app already has for that
   phone number.** On-device, no backend or upload needed — this is the
   "you already know what they look like from your own address book" case,
   and should win whenever it's actually set, since it's the picture the
   user themself chose to associate with that contact.
   **Status: implemented.** `fe/store/contacts/adapter.ts` reads
   `contact.image?.uri` from `expo-contacts` into `Contact.avatar_url`;
   `shared/store/contacts/index.ts`'s `fetchContacts` keeps it device-local
   (never sent to the backend) and re-attaches it to each contact after
   the `/api/enrich_contacts` round trip, keyed by phone. `ContactCard` and
   `calling-screen.tsx` already render it
   (`contact.avatar_url || contact.app_avatar_url`).
2. **The avatar the other person set for themselves in-app**
   (`Contact.app_avatar_url`, uploaded by them, served from wherever we end
   up storing it — S3 or similar). Falls back to this when the local
   device doesn't have a photo for that number.
   **Status: blocked on S3**, see below.
3. **Placeholder** (initials or generic icon) if neither of the above is
   available. Already implemented in `ContactCardPresentation` and in the
   dead upload UI in `settings.tsx`.

## Existing dead code to be aware of

`fe/app/(app)/(home)/settings.tsx` already has an avatar upload UI
(`uploadAvatar`, image picker, placeholder-with-initials fallback) left over
from an earlier attempt. It's currently non-functional:

- It calls `POST /api/upload_avatar`, which does not exist anywhere in
  `be/app` — no route, no handler.
- `User.avatar_url` is referenced in `fe/store/auth.ts`, but the backend
  `User` model has no `avatar_url` column — nothing persists it.

When implementing priority #2 (self-set in-app avatar), reuse/fix that UI
rather than building a new one from scratch.

## Feature

Let a user set their own avatar. When displaying a contact (in the contacts
list, and on the incoming/outgoing call screen), resolve the image to show
with this priority:

1. **The photo the device's native Contacts app already has for that
   phone number.** On-device, no backend or upload needed — this is the
   "you already know what they look like from your own address book" case,
   and should win whenever it's actually set, since it's the picture the
   user themself chose to associate with that contact.

   `calling-screen.tsx` already render it

# Call signaling: three approaches compared

Three different designs exist for how a call offer reaches an offline (or
not-yet-ready) callee, and what happens if it doesn't arrive right away.
This compares `main` (current), `experiment/drop-pending-call-buffering`,
and `fix/shared-module-types`.

## `main` (current)

`callUser()` sends the WebRTC offer over WS immediately
(`fe/store/calls.ts`). If the callee is offline, the backend
(`be/app/ws/manager.py`'s `pending_calls`/`pending_candidates`, wired up in
`be/app/ws/routes.py`) buffers the offer and its ICE candidates in memory
and replays them to the callee once they connect, with a 60s expiry
(`CALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`) after which the caller's availability is restored
and the pending offer is dropped.

- No client-side retry — one offer sent, buffered server-side if needed.
- Simple, but: in-memory buffering means a backend restart drops all
  in-flight offers; stale ICE candidates can accumulate for a call that
  never completes within the window; no idempotency guarantees on
  accept/reject/cancel (whatever's implemented is ad hoc per handler).

## `experiment/drop-pending-call-buffering`

Removes the server-side buffering entirely (`manager.py`'s
`pending_calls`/`pending_candidates` and the queue/take/expire methods are
deleted). If the callee isn't connected, the backend just replies
`user_offline` — no state kept. The **caller's client** takes over:
`startOfferRetry()`/`sendOfferRetry()` resend the offer every 4s
(`OFFER_RETRY_INTERVAL`), up to 15 attempts (`MAX_OFFER_ATTEMPTS`), with an
ICE restart every 8th attempt (`ICE_RESTART_EVERY`) to recover from a
network change mid-ring (Wi-Fi -> cellular). Also fixes two bugs around
restoring caller/callee availability on WebSocket disconnect and
pending-offer expiry.

- Smallest diff (4 files), no DB migration, easy to test in isolation.
- Moves the "who's responsible for retrying" question from the server
  (buffer + replay) to the client (resend on a timer) — no server memory
  leak risk, no restart-drops-calls risk.
- Known issue (documented in `CALL_RETRY_KNOWN_ISSUES.md`): most retries
  resend the same SDP so any answer to them is fine, but the periodic
  ICE-restart genuinely regenerates the offer (new ICE ufrag/pwd). An
  answer to a pre-restart offer arriving after the restart has already
  replaced `pc.localDescription` gets applied against mismatched ICE
  credentials — a narrow race, only around the ~32s restart boundary, not
  fixed in that branch.

## `fix/shared-module-types`

A full protocol redesign across `be/`, `fe/`, and `web/`, documented in its
own `CALL_SIGNALING_FLOW.md`. Introduces a `CallInvite` DB model
(`be/alembic/versions/0002_call_invites.py`) and moves call *lifecycle*
(invite/accept/reject/cancel/end) onto REST endpoints, idempotent by
`call_uuid`, with a 60s ringing TTL and push fallback when the target is
offline. WebSocket becomes a pure relay — no offer/ICE buffering at all.

The key structural change: the caller does **not** create a WebRTC offer
until the callee has explicitly sent `callee_ready` over WS, confirming
they're actually online and ready to receive it. Only then does the caller
create the offer, exactly once — no retry loop, no regeneration, so the
ICE-restart race in the retry-loop design can't occur by construction.

REST calls run in parallel with, not instead of, the live WS signaling: the
answer/callee_ready/offer/ICE messages are still sent directly over WS
between clients, same as today; REST is only used for durable
lifecycle bookkeeping and the offline-push fallback path (checked via
`manager.is_connected(phone)` — no push is sent if the target already has
an open WS connection). So it doesn't add REST-latency to the
already-online case.

- Removes the offer-before-ready race by construction rather than papering
  over it with retries.
- Much bigger surface area: new table, rewritten REST contract, needs
  validating across all three clients at once before it's safe to merge
  (a real test-merge into `main` conflicts on 10 files, since `main`'s
  current call code evolved independently since the fork point).

## Where things stand

`experiment/drop-pending-call-buffering` is the one actively being tested
(low risk, narrow scope, backend behavior toggle still undecided). If it
holds up, `fix/shared-module-types`'s `callee_ready` handshake is the
natural next step to actually close the race it works around, rather than
retry past it.

`be/app/ws/routes.py`) buffers the offer and its ICE candidates in memory
and replays them to the callee once they connect, with a 60s expiry
(`CALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`) after which the caller's availability is restored
and the pending offer is dropped.

- No client-side retry — one offer sent, buffered server-side if needed.
- Simple, but: in-memory buffering means a backend restart drops all
  in-flight offers; stale ICE candidates can accumulate for a call that
  never completes within the window; no idempotency guarantees on
  accept/reject/cancel (whatever's implemented is ad hoc per handler).

## `experiment/drop-pending-call-buffering`

Removes the server-side buffering entirely (`manager.py`'s
`pending_calls`/`pending_candidates` and the queue/take/expire methods are
deleted). If the callee isn't connected, the backend just replies
`user_offline` — no state kept. The **caller's client** takes over:
`startOfferRetry()`/`sendOfferRetry()` resend the offer every 4s
(`OFFER_RETRY_INTERVAL`), up to 15 attempts (`MAX_OFFER_ATTEMPTS`), with an
ICE restart every 8th attempt (`ICE_RESTART_EVERY`) to recover from a
network change mid-ring (Wi-Fi -> cellular). Also fixes two bugs around
restoring caller/callee availability on WebSocket disconnect and
pending-offer expiry.

- Smallest diff (4 files), no DB migration, easy to test in isolation.
- Moves the "who's responsible for retrying" question from the server
  (buffer + replay) to the client (resend on a timer) — no server memory
  leak risk, no restart-drops-calls risk.
- Known issue (documented in `CALL_RETRY_KNOWN_ISSUES.md`): most retries
  resend the same SDP so any answer to them is fine, but the periodic
  ICE-restart genuinely regenerates the offer (new ICE ufrag/pwd). An
  answer to a pre-restart offer arriving after the restart has already
  replaced `pc.localDescription` gets applied against mismatched ICE
  credentials — a narrow race, only around the ~32s restart boundary, not
  fixed in that branch.

## `fix/shared-module-types`

A full protocol redesign across `be/`, `fe/`, and `web/`, documented in its
own `CALL_SIGNALING_FLOW.md`. Introduces a `CallInvite` DB model
(`be/alembic/versions/0002_call_invites.py`) and moves call *lifecycle*
(invite/accept/reject/cancel/end) onto REST endpoints, idempotent by
`call_uuid`, with a 60s ringing TTL and push fallback when the target is
offline. WebSocket becomes a pure relay — no offer/ICE buffering at all.

The key structural change: the caller does **not** create a WebRTC offer
until the callee has explicitly sent `callee_ready` over WS, confirming
they're actually online and ready to receive it. Only then does the caller
create the offer, exactly once — no retry loop, no regeneration, so the
ICE-restart race in the retry-loop design can't occur by construction.

REST calls run in parallel with, not instead of, the live WS signaling: the
answer/callee_ready/offer/ICE messages are still sent directly over WS
between clients, same as today; REST is only used for durable
lifecycle bookkeeping and the offline-push fallback path (checked via
`manager.is_connected(phone)` — no push is sent if the target already has
an open WS connection). So it doesn't add REST-latency to the
already-online case.

- Removes the offer-before-ready race by construction rather than papering
  over it with retries.
- Much bigger surface area: new table, rewritten REST contract, needs
  validating across all three clients at once before it's safe to merge
  (a real test-merge into `main` conflicts on 10 files, since `main`'s
  current call code evolved independently since the fork point).

## Where things stand

`experiment/drop-pending-call-buffering` is the one actively being tested
(low risk, narrow scope, backend behavior toggle still undecided). If it
holds up, `fix/shared-module-types`'s `callee_ready` handshake is the
natural next step to actually close the race it works around, rather than
retry past it.
